question: When is it legal to drive off the road to pass another vehicle?
options: It is not legal under any conditions
When the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a wide paved shoulder
When traffic is stopped on a two-lane highway
When instructed by another driver waving you past
explanation: Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass another vehicle under any conditions.

question: Which of the following is the proper procedure for parallel parking?
options: Pull straight into the space nose-first and then back up to straighten out
Stop next to the vehicle in front of the open space, and then back into the space
Stop next to the vehicle behind the open space, and then pull forward into the space
Back into the space at a 90-degree angle until your rear tires hit the curb
explanation: To parallel park, pull up alongside the vehicle in front of the open space (about two feet away) and then back into the space at about a 45-degree angle.

question: What speed should you be driving when entering onto a highway?
options: At least 10 mph slower than highway traffic
At or near the speed of traffic
Exactly 45 mph on all on-ramps
As fast as your vehicle can accelerate regardless of traffic
explanation: When entering a highway, you should be at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge safely.

question: Who can legally park next to a curb painted blue?
options: Anyone stopping for less than 5 minutes to pick up passengers
Commercial delivery vehicles unloading freight
A person who is disabled and has a special placard or vehicle license plate for disabled persons
Any senior driver aged 62 or older
explanation: Blue curbs are reserved exclusively for disabled persons or someone driving a disabled person who displays a special placard or disabled license plate.

question: In addition to setting your parking brake, what should you do when parking on a hill?
options: Leave the vehicle in neutral so the brakes do not lock
Turn on your emergency flashers until you return
Make sure your vehicle is in the 'park' position or in gear
Leave at least 3 feet between your wheels and the curb
explanation: When parking on a hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in the 'park' position (or in gear for a manual transmission).

question: Where should you begin a left turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street?
options: The center lane
The far-left lane
Any lane as long as no bicyclists are present
The lane closest to the right curb
explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start the turn from the far-left lane.

question: What color curb does not allow vehicles to stop, stand, or park (except buses at a marked bus zone)?
options: White
Green
Yellow
Red
explanation: A red curb indicates no stopping, standing, or parking, except for buses at a red zone marked for buses only.

question: When is parking in a crosshatched (diagonal lines) area next to a disabled parking space allowed?
options: When you have a valid disabled parking placard and all blue spaces are full
When waiting inside your vehicle for less than 3 minutes
It is never allowed to park in a crosshatched (diagonal lines) area
Only on Sundays and holidays
explanation: It is never legal to park or leave your vehicle in the crosshatched (diagonal lines) area next to a designated disabled parking space.

question: In which lane should you end your turn when making a right turn?
options: Any lane that is open
The lane closest to the center divider
The lane closest to the right edge of the road
The bicycle lane
explanation: Begin and end a right turn in the lane closest to the right edge of the road without swinging wide into another lane.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when there is a school bus ahead that starts flashing yellow warning lights?
options: Speed up to pass the bus before the red lights turn on
Slow down and prepare to stop
Honk your horn to alert children on the sidewalk
Change lanes and pass at 25 mph
explanation: School buses flash yellow lights when preparing to stop to let children off; you must slow down and prepare to stop.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when reaching an intersection where a person operating a motorized wheelchair has entered the crosswalk?
options: Turn carefully behind the motorized wheelchair before it reaches the curb
Remain stopped behind the crosswalk line until the motorized wheelchair has safely finished crossing
Tap your horn lightly to let the person know you are waiting
Proceed slowly through the other half of the crosswalk
explanation: A person with a disability using a motorized wheelchair is a pedestrian; you must remain stopped behind the limit/crosswalk line until they have safely finished crossing.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: Any driver who willfully flees or attempts to evade law enforcement, during which a person is seriously injured, is subject to:
options: A fine of no more than $500 and traffic violator school
License suspension for 30 days only
Imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years, or a county jail for one year or less
Community service for 60 hours
explanation: A person convicted of causing serious bodily injury during a law enforcement pursuit is subject to imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years, or a county jail for one year or less.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do who is stopped at an intersection and wants to make a left turn?
options: Turn immediately before oncoming traffic enters the intersection
Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian or approaching vehicle that is close enough to be dangerous
Flash high-beam headlights to claim the right-of-way
Expect oncoming traffic turning right to yield to you
explanation: When turning left, you must check for pedestrians and give the right-of-way to any pedestrian or approaching vehicle that is close enough to be dangerous.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: Pull into the middle of the intersection so you do not miss the green light
Follow closely behind the car ahead and stop in the crosswalk
Wait and do not enter the intersection until your vehicle can get completely across
Use the bicycle lane to drive around the blocked traffic
explanation: Even with a green light, it is against the law to enter or block an intersection unless there is enough space to completely cross before the light turns red.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: When is it required for you to obey directions from a school crossing guard?
options: Only during posted school zone hours
Only when children are visible in the middle of the street
At all times
Only when flashing yellow school zone lights are active
explanation: When near schools, you must look for school safety patrols or crossing guards and obey their directions at all times.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when traffic is slow and heavy, and you must cross railroad tracks before reaching an upcoming intersection?
options: Stop on the tracks briefly if the cars ahead are moving slowly
Wait until you can completely cross the tracks before proceeding
Drive around the crossing gates if no train is visible
Speed up to close the gap with the car in front of you
explanation: Never stop on railroad tracks; wait and do not begin proceeding across the tracks unless you have enough room to completely clear them.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal light direct a driver to do?
options: Come to a complete stop before entering the intersection
Slow down and proceed with caution
Speed up before the signal turns red
Yield to all vehicles on the left and right after stopping
explanation: A flashing yellow traffic signal light is a warning to slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop.

question: According to California's Basic Speed Law, if a highway has a posted speed limit of 65 mph, what does this mean?
options: You may legally drive 65 mph regardless of weather or traffic
You must drive 65 mph only if driving conditions are ideal, and you can be given a speeding ticket at the posted limit if road or weather conditions require a slower speed
65 mph is the minimum speed allowed in all lanes
You cannot be cited for speeding as long as you stay at or below 65 mph
explanation: Under California's Basic Speed Law, you may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions; 65 mph is the maximum limit only under ideal conditions.

question: At what point during a rainfall are roads most slippery, especially on a hot and dry day?
options: After it has been raining steadily for several hours
For the first several minutes when it starts to rain
Only after the rain has completely stopped
Only when water puddles are more than 2 inches deep
explanation: Pavement is most slippery during the first several minutes of rain, especially after dry, hot weather, because oil and dust on the road surface have not yet been washed away.

question: What should an adult driver do if their cell phone rings while driving and they do not have a hands-free device?
options: Answer the call briefly on speakerphone while holding the phone
Do not answer the phone and let the call go to voicemail
Check the caller ID and send a quick text reply
Slow down to 25 mph in the right lane to answer the call
explanation: Driving while using a handheld cell phone is unsafe and illegal; do not answer your cell phone if it rings and let the call go to voicemail.

sectionTitle: Section 10: Financial Responsibility, Insurance Requirements, and Collisions
question: According to the California Driver's Handbook, what is one of the most common causes of traffic collisions?
options: Mechanical tire failure
Driver distractions
Road construction detours
Driving vehicles with automatic transmissions
explanation: Driver distractions, unsafe speed, improper turns, and failing to follow right-of-way or stop rules are the most common causes of collisions.
